labels.notes: Still unmarked. The ledger regex (tools/ledger.py docstring_label_re, ``**`label`**``) finds no mark anywhere in the file, and the REPORT row is partial with marked: false, as the dispatch requires. NoCircuitStatement K (l.738) is unchanged: ∀ ε ≥ 1/10^14, ∀ x, IsCircuit ε x → x ∈ K, with K a parameter. It is a Prop, it is not proved, and nothing claims it is. Matveev's theorem enters only as the Props NoCircuitMatveev C and NoCircuitMatveevAbs C (l.486, l.491). Both are defs, with no axiom: `axiom` occurs only twice in the file, both times in prose (« never an axiom », l.47 and l.485). The AUDIT-1 major is resolved. noCircuit_of_cited (l.776–783) now reads `∃ B, (∀ x, IsCircuit ε x → minimalPeriod T x ≤ B) ∧ ∀ K, (∀ x, IsCircuit ε x → minimalPeriod T x ≤ B → x ∈ K) → ∀ x, IsCircuit ε x → x ∈ K`. B is chosen before K. The first conjunct is a bound with no antecedent, so the choice of B can no longer falsify a hypothesis. The second conjunct follows from the first in one line, and the docstring says the content is the first conjunct. The proof term is `obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := noCircuit_period_bounded hC hM hε`. hM passes through noCircuit_period_bounded_of's hlow into noCircuit_l244_of_lower, the only place a lower bound on |2^{p_n} − 3^n| is used. So the bound rests on noCircuit_period_bounded and on Matveev's theorem. Without hM the bound is not free. tauto, aesop, by_contra/push Not/simp_all, ⟨0, simp_all [IsCircuit]⟩ and grind all fail on `∃ B, ∀ x, IsCircuit ε x → minimalPeriod T x ≤ B` under hε alone. The abstract shape `∀ P f, ∃ B, ∀ x, P x → f x ≤ B` is refutable, and the probe refuted it at P = True, f = Int.toNat. The old shape `∃ B, (∀ x, P x → f x ≤ B → Q x) → ∀ x, P x → Q x` is provable for every P, Q, f, and the probe proved it, which confirms AUDIT-1 and the new docstring's description. Mathematically, the only elementary lower bound is |2^{p_n} − 3^n| ≥ 1. With it, noCircuit_upper gives 3^{q+1}2^n ≤ 2·3^n·4^n, which bounds no n when ε ≤ log₃ 6 ≈ 1.63. For ε > 1 the bound is elementary, since a run of p ≥ n forces x = −1. The content therefore lies in ε ∈ (log₃(3/2), 1], where Baker-type input is needed. That interval contains real circuits: (−5, −7) up to ε = 1 and −17 up to ε = 4/7. The probe derived, from noCircuit_of_cited at ε = 4/7 > log₃(3/2), a B ≥ 7 (the least period of −17), so the bound conjunct is not vacuous. hC is implied by hM: P = n = 1 gives e^C ≥ 2. It is harmless, and it narrows nothing.

major_resolved.evidence: New statement at l.776–780, with the bound as the first conjunct and B before K. It is proved from noCircuit_period_bounded hC hM hε. Five tactic attempts without hM fail, and the abstract bound shape is refuted. No other declaration has the « ∃ B before an implication whose antecedent depends on B » shape. The file has seven existentials. One is a proof-internal obtain (l.143). Four are bounds with B before x or n and no B-dependent antecedent: noCircuit_eventually l.622, noCircuit_period_bounded_of l.661, noCircuit_period_bounded l.701 and _pos l.716. noCircuit_l236_false (l.1033) is an eventual statement, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, …. The last is noCircuit_of_cited itself (l.778). The docstring (l.770–775), SCOPE (l.60–65) and REPORT findings[0] say that the earlier form was vacuous and that the content is the bound. kb_proposals[5] records the lesson.

minor_fixes_checked: « largest term »: dropped from SCOPE Finding 3 (l.75–80), which now says « can be nonzero (at −17 with i = 6, q = 3 it is −224 of the total −278) ». REPORT findings[4] adds that the term is not the largest in general. Recomputed in exact integer arithmetic over the orbit −17, −25, −37, −55, −41, −61, −91 (a = 1,1,1,2,1,1,4). At i = 6, q = 3 the terms are (−54, 0, 0, −224), sum −278, and 27·(−278) = −7506 = A_9 − A_10. At i = 3, q = 2 they are (−1134, 0, 0, 0, −256), sum −1390, and 9·(−1390) = −12510 = A_5 − A_6. At i = 0, q = 2, where the run extends left, they are (−162, 0, 0, −672, 0), with last term 0, as the REPORT says. The two term lists and the i = 3 identity were also checked by `decide` against the strict Aun and seq17 in the probe.

l.236 threshold in three bases. The condition 2·log_b 3·(3^η − 1) < 1 is η < log₃(1 + 1/(2 log_b 3)), which is 0.341420 (ln), 0.652496 (log₁₀) and 0.249579 (log₂). These are the printed 0.341, 0.652 and 0.250 in SCOPE Finding 4 (l.87–89), in the noCircuit_l236_false docstring (l.1026–1027), in REPORT findings[6] and in questions[3]. The Lean hypothesis is in Real.log, so 0.341 is the one tied to the statement, as the text says.

summary: Round 2 is clean. The AUDIT-1 major is resolved. noCircuit_of_cited now carries the uniform least-period bound as its first conjunct, with B fixed before K. The proof gets the bound from noCircuit_period_bounded, and through it from the Matveev hypothesis. Without that hypothesis the bound does not fall to classical logic or to automation (tauto, aesop, simp_all, grind all fail). The abstract bound shape is refutable, while the old shape is a provable tautology, and both facts were proved in the probe. No other declaration has the « ∃ B before a B-dependent antecedent » shape. The four minor fixes are made and true: the example terms and the three log-base thresholds were recomputed exactly and by decide. The file typechecks under -DwarningAsError=true with 0 sorry, 0 native_decide and no axiom declaration. #print axioms on all 51 declarations gives only the standard three. NoCircuit.lean and CitedSteps.lean elaborate together over the whole strict root with no name clash. Nothing outside the dispatch was touched.
